releaseNotes: Platform release: an account can be signed in on more than one device. Signing in used to delete every other session for that account, so opening Formation on a phone silently signed you out on the laptop you were working on — a bug nothing reported because it looked like an ordinary expiry. Sessions now accumulate up to a bound of ten, the least recently used going first, and each carries a coarse device label — "Chrome on macOS" — derived from the user-agent and stored instead of it, because a browser build string is a fingerprint and the label is only there so someone can recognise their own devices. The engine's state, reducer, and catalog are untouched; this manifest advances only to keep root package parity.

The account's own security surface in the same release: a page listing every device holding a live session, with the current one marked, any device signable out from any other, and one action to sign out everywhere else. Changing a password requires the current password even from a signed-in session — a session someone else walked up to must not be enough to take the account — is rate limited like any other guessing, and signs out every other device, because the reason to change a password is usually that one of them should not have it. Nothing on the surface takes an identifier that could name another person's account. Checks, 89 domain tests, the production build, and the full audit pass.
